title: Schilling, Johnny Fisher and musicians who drink
summary: Allen asks about Hacker Schilling and George Schilling and trumpeter Johnny Fisher, who lost jobs through drinking; Duerr talks about his own sleeping trouble.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well I know you would have gone for a while. What about bands like Schilling? Did you know Hacker Schilling then?
Yeah I knew the old man, yeah I knew him. And I worked with his son George at one job there and I knew George for years, like later on I used to lead him down in the union and stuff like that.
And Fisher, Johnny Fisher, did you know him? Johnny Fisher?
Well Johnny Fisher, is that the Johnny Fisher that came from New York that you're talking about?
The clarinet play. Oh no, no, no.
He still lives down on North Park.
I know Burgundy now. Burgundy, I think. No, I don't think I knew him. He played clarinet? He played clarinet.
There was a Johnny Fisher, a trumpet player, around New York.

He played pretty good trumpet. He played with some pretty good band but he was on the blues tour a little bit. Well he came down here later and then he went to the Gulf Coast. Well I don't know where he is. But he and Jack Miranda. You knew John the Fisher that I'm talking about? Yeah, with Jack Miranda and all those guys down here. I knew him in New York for years.
